violation_description: Following SET audits of seven professionally certified applications submitted by Professional Engineer Mohammad Billah that presented major violations of Code and Rules, SET offered a voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and Directive 14 privileges for multiple failed audits, which the Engineer signed on December 9, 2021. Subsequently, the Engineer was subject to an internal SET audit of applicants who had surrendered Directive 14 final inspection privileges. SET discovered that while his privileges were surrendered, the Engineer submitted TR-1: Technical Report Statement of Responsibility forms to certify performance and sign-off of thirty (30) Directive 14 final inspections. SET filed a petition at OATH for false statements and before trial, and the Engineer signed a Stipulation of Settlement that included a two-year voluntary surrender of all filing privileges and permanent voluntary surrender of Professional Certification and Directive 14/Final Inspection privileges, which took effect on August 13, 2025.

violation_description: at 461 Park Avenue South related to a large advertising sign were sustained upon appeal. The summonses were for work without a permit, owner acting as an Outdoor Advertising Company (“OAC”) without registration, failure to engage a licensed sign hanger, failure to post the required UL decal, and for advertising signs prohibited under the Zoning Resolution. Following the Respondent’s arguments, the Appeals Board found that the advertising sign’s size had changed significantly over the years so a legal nonconforming use defense was not established. The Board also held that the sign being prohibited in a zoning district is not a defense to a work without a permit charge
enforcement_text: Summonses issued to Gammon Enterprizes LLC issued at 461 Park Avenue South related to a large advertising sign were sustained upon appeal. The summonses were for work without a permit, owner acting as an Outdoor Advertising Company (“OAC”) without registration, failure to engage a licensed sign hanger, failure to post the required UL decal, and for advertising signs prohibited under the Zoning Resolution. Following the Respondent’s arguments, the Appeals Board found that the advertising sign’s size had changed significantly over the years so a legal nonconforming use defense was not established. The Board also held that the sign being prohibited in a zoning district is not a defense to a work without a permit charge.
